title: SB 2774 (2012 Regular Session): Voter identification; require those who appear to vote to present proper.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 1(1)
(quote) Each person who shall appear to vote in person at a polling place or the registrar's office shall be required to identify himself or herself to an election manager or the registrar by presenting current and valid photo identification before such person shall be allowed to vote.
(section) Sec. 1(2)
(quote) The identification required by subsection (1) of this section shall include, but not be limited to, the following: (a) A current and valid Mississippi driver's license; (b) A current and valid identification card issued by a branch, department, agency or entity of the State of Mississippi; (c) A current and valid United States passport;
(section) Sec. 1(2)
(quote) (f) A valid tribal identification card containing a photograph of the elector; and (g) A current and valid United States military identification card.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 1(3)
(quote) A person who appears to vote in person at a polling place and does not have identification as required by this section may vote by affidavit ballot. The affidavit ballot shall then be counted if the person shall present acceptable photo identification to the registrar within five (5) calendar days after the election, not including Saturdays, Sundays or holidays.
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) Conforming 23-15-631(3)
(quote) The Secretary of State shall prepare instructions on how absent voters may comply with the identification requirements of Section 1 of this act.
(section) Conforming 23-15-719
(quote) The registrar shall identify the applicant by requiring him to present identification as required by Section 1 of this act, and shall then deliver the ballots to the applicant by mail or to the applicant in the registrar's office.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) Sec. 1(5)
(quote) The intentional failure of an election official to require a voter to present identification as required by this section shall be considered corrupt conduct under Section 97-13-19 and shall be reported to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.
(other) Sec. 1(4): intimidating a voter by using the section is punished by fine of $5,000 to $25,000 and/or 1-5 years
(other) Conforming: 23-15-11, 23-15-541, 23-15-631, 23-15-639, 23-15-719
(other) Vote certification not sooner than 5 calendar days after the election (23-15-597, 599, 601, 603, 607)
(other) Preclearance
